report:
PASS for the entire partial operator manuscript, with the routine normalization clarification below. This does not solve, close, or narrow the unchanged original P16.4 equation problem. No material mathematical defect or essential unresolved premise remains in the operator argument.

The established domain is exactly: complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean K, including trivial, discrete and nondiscrete valuations; smooth geometrically integral projective X; an actual ample rational line bundle L; a continuous psh reference; and actual all-point decreasing-FS-net endpoints of finite majorant energy. In every dimension, the construction gives canonical positive mixed Radon measures of raw mass V=(L^n), all-E1 test integrability, joint decreasing weighted continuity, the displayed energy identity, affine-segment polynomial differentiation, reference covariance and complete-field pullback/pushforward covariance. Affine dependence is understood on admissible convex combinations of curvature slots.

I independently retrieved the specified [BE v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3) and [CLD v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1). I checked the complete pertinent FS, PL, closure, regularization, continuous mixed-calculus and energy proof units, including their applications here. The ledger's prior-reading assertions and hashes were not used as mathematical evidence. The external premises below have zero-based primary-source bindings. Compact Hausdorff normality, lattice Stone–Weierstrass and positive-functional Riesz representation are used in their ordinary precise domains; the additional net-integration assertions are reconstructed, not assumed. The original problem's historical discussion serves only the separate completion-scope audit.

The cone is genuinely the fixed-bundle, pointwise decreasing-FS-net cone. It retains supported points and literal minus-infinity values. A defining continuous majorant makes each scalar potential bounded above, and the majorant infimum cannot be plus infinity. Rational convex combinations follow directly from products of FS systems after clearing denominators. Real coefficients follow by uniform approximation. Uniform closure can be reconstructed by selecting a summable-error subsequence and adding decreasing constant corrections. Abstract decreasing closure follows by ordering continuous approximants with positive constant slack, using the compact majorant argument to obtain a common smaller approximant. Equal approximants can be identified, or the index set treated as a directed preorder. None of this invokes divisorial finiteness.

Smooth regularization applies to the finitely many metrics simultaneously on a product index set. Regularized maxima give convex smooth local weights; their insensitivity to sufficiently small coordinates handles vanishing sections. Continuous endpoints yield uniform convergence by compact Dini reasoning. In CLD normalization, Stokes gives −∫f dd^c f Q=∫d′f∧d″f∧Q≥0. The carrier is good, separated and boundaryless, and compactness supplies the required support condition. Products of positive (1,1)-forms are strongly positive, so the sign is correct. Green's identity gives symmetry. Every signed curvature expression has a finite expansion into positive measures with fixed intersection masses; consequently its total variation is uniformly bounded. Uniform convergence of scalar factors and weak convergence of these signed measures therefore pass the Dirichlet identities to continuous data. Cancellation in the multiadditive metric calculus establishes representation independence. Positivity of the smooth quadratic expressions, followed by this passage, also justifies Cauchy–Schwarz for every real scalar coefficient.

The continuous energy calculus can be reconstructed directly. Differentiating its finite sum and integrating by parts makes the intermediate terms telescope, leaving E′(u_t)=∫(v−u)θ_{u_t}^n. Integrating the binomial expansion along a segment gives the relative energy-gap formula, with coefficient 1/(n+1) in every term. This establishes the cocycle, monotonicity, constant law and V-Lipschitz bound without an E1 input. Differentiating once more gives E″(u_t)=−nD_{θ_{u_t}^{n−1}}(v−u,v−u)≤0.

For the ordered weak estimate, write δ=v−u≥0 and Q_j=θ_u^jθ_v^{n−1−j}. The exact identities are ∑_jD_{Q_j}(δ,δ)=∫δ(θ_u^n−θ_v^n)≥0 and ∑_jD_{Q_j}(f,δ)=−∫f(θ_v^n−θ_u^n). The first sum is at most ∫δθ_u^n, hence at most (n+1)(E(v)−E(u)). Writing f=h−k on a common ample A gives D_{Q_j}(f,f)≤2||f||∞(A·L^{n−1})=C_f. Cauchy–Schwarz first in each form and then over the n indices yields exactly √(n(n+1)C_f(E(v)−E(u))). The density condition holds at trivial valuation because the weight group used is R, not the zero group.

Decreasing energy continuity is valid for arbitrary directed nets. For a continuous majorant v of the endpoint and ε>0, the closed sets {u_i≥v+ε} are decreasing and have empty intersection. Compactness makes one of them empty, proving the required tail bound and then equality with the majorant infimum. This also proves convergence to minus infinity when endpoint energy is minus infinity. Separately, an identically-minus-infinity limit forces tails below every constant −M+ε, so their energies tend to minus infinity. Continuous concavity supplies a finite lower energy bound for convex combinations of finite-energy endpoints. That independent constant argument excludes an identically-minus-infinity convex limit before admitting it to the actual E1 cone.

The Radon lemma is sound without metrizability. At each strict level, the directed union of open superlevel sets has measure equal to the supremum of their measures, by inner regularity and finite subcovers of compact subsets. Finite lower layer sums and one common index establish increasing-LSC net integration, including infinite integrals. For Portmanteau, normality supplies continuous minorants supported in finitely many strict open levels; their integrals approximate the LSC integral from below. Passing each minorant through weak convergence proves the stated net liminf inequality. No arbitrary measurable-net monotone-convergence theorem is used.

For a continuous approximation of u∈E1, finite decreasing energy convergence makes each PL-test integral a Cauchy net; a common upper index handles incomparable indices. Uniform mass bounds extend convergence to all continuous tests, and the limiting positive bounded functional has a unique Radon representative of mass V. Maximum product nets prove approximation independence. For ordered singular u≤v, the maximum of their two approximating nets decreases to v, so the continuous estimate passes with energy gap E(v)−E(u). This establishes the singular ordered estimate and decreasing pure weak continuity.

The mixed polarization coefficients are correct. Inclusion–exclusion cancels every degree-n monomial missing a label. The sole surviving label pattern uses each of the n labels once, with coefficient n!, and the corresponding scalar coefficient sum is n!. Every subset average lies in the already established E1 cone. Simultaneous continuous approximations turn the signed polarization formula into positive genuine mixed measures at every stage. Their weak limit is therefore positive and has mass V. Symmetry, affine identities and arbitrary decreasing mixed weak continuity follow from finite continuous identities and subset-average limits.

The all-test averaging coefficient is exactly n!/(n+1)^(n+2): n! curvature permutations, n curvature denominators, one weight denominator and one energy denominator. All other terms retained in B(z) are nonnegative. Concavity consequently gives the claimed factor C_n=(n+1)^(n+1)/n! multiplying B(w)+∑B(u_r). Continuous weights pass through mixed weak limits; increasing-LSC integration then passes to the actual unbounded weight.

A routine normalization clarification is necessary here: merely nonpositive endpoints do not themselves justify choosing nonpositive defining approximants in the original reference. The manuscript's stated common-reference normalization is sufficient when made explicit with ε>0. Compactness puts all approximating tails below ε. Replace the reference by ψ+ε and every scalar by its value minus ε. The already available continuous cocycle, infimized over the same absolute majorants, changes each cost to B(q)+εV and leaves all curvature measures unchanged. The proof then gives ∫(−w)MA+εV≤C_n[B(w)+∑B(u_r)+(n+1)εV]. Letting ε decrease to zero proves the displayed bound exactly. This uses existing arguments and adds neither an envelope hypothesis nor a constrained-approximation theorem. Finite integrability immediately gives pole-nullness for each E1 test. Only finite collections of full-measure finite-value sets are subsequently intersected.

The singular-test error constant is also exact. The top term of the ordered energy gap contributes 1/(n+1); h_k−h_j contributes 1/2; and the positive expansion of MA(h_k) dominates 2^(−n)MA(u). These give A_n=2^(n+1)(n+1). Increasing continuous differences pass to the singular weight by the Radon lemma. For singular u, w_k−w is nonnegative LSC, so Portmanteau bounds the endpoint integral by the liminf. Both energies converge separately to finite numbers. Their difference therefore converges without infinity subtraction.

For fixed-weight continuity, the product net (u_i+w_k)/2 decreases to its finite-energy endpoint. Its energy convergence gives one common pair of tail indices controlling the test error uniformly in i, including the limit output. Weak convergence handles the fixed continuous test. For moving weights, compactness gives w_i≤w_k+η eventually, so the additional error is bounded by the preceding test error plus ηV. All relevant integrals are finite by the previously proved proposition. Applying this result to the finitely many subset-average nets proves the complete mixed weighted law on arbitrary common directed index sets.

The genuine singular energy formula follows term by term using the moving-weight law and decreasing energy continuity. For an affine E1 segment, every approximating derivative is a degree-at-most-n polynomial with finitely many binomial mixed-integral coefficients. Weighted continuity passes each coefficient to a finite value; the energy's constant term tends to E(u). Integrating the coefficient limits gives a polynomial of degree at most n+1, whose pointwise values equal the majorant energy by decreasing continuity. Its derivative is the asserted integral. Pole-nullness supplies the finite-value representatives for u and v for each output, including the one-sided endpoint formulas; no uncountable common full-measure set or subtraction of infinities is required.

Reference covariance is an exact bijection of absolute continuous majorants followed by the continuous cocycle and an infimum. Thus E_{ψ′}(u−b)=E_ψ(u)−E_ψ(b), and the absolute approximation measures are identical. The complete-field laws apply in the required domains. Pullback preserves FS approximation and its all-point endpoint; projection surjectivity preserves nontriviality. The smooth field-law calculation uses canonical tropical calibration by finite-flat degrees on generic Gauss fibers, whose ranks survive scalar extension. Passing through uniform approximation gives the continuous mixed pushforward law; testing singular limits with f∘p gives the displayed singular law. Continuous energy covariance and decreasing energy continuity then give exact singular energy covariance. Intersection degree is unchanged, so there is no field-degree factor. No extension-supnorm identity or descent of arbitrary upstairs singular metrics is used.

In dimension zero, smooth geometric integrality forces X=Spec K: a nontrivial finite separable extension would split after geometric base change. The analytic carrier is one point, a non-identically-minus-infinity scalar is finite, and V=1, E(u)=u and the empty mixed product is the unit point mass. All stated identities follow directly.

Harmless source/proof wording corrections were checked explicitly. The last expanded summand in BE Lemma 8.6 must have a minus sign; the correct identity still gives its stated absolute-value bound. The uniform-closure argument needs a summable-error subsequence before adding decreasing constants. The nonpositive-approximant wording needs the ε-normalization just detailed. These change no claimed domain, operator, coefficient or bound and require no substantial replacement argument.

The unchanged original equation gaps remain: strict Borel locality and comparison; compactness of normalized actual potentials; general-field envelope continuity or suitable replacements; orthogonality and both-sign differentiation in outer continuous directions; a precise target finite-energy/finite-dual characterization beyond output-test integrability; attainment for arbitrary admissible prescribed positive Radon targets of mass V; and uniqueness modulo constants for every solution. Canonical approximation independence is not equation uniqueness. The partial manuscript proves an operator component and its calculus, while the original existence-and-uniqueness completion criteria remain unmet.

premises: For a separated projective scheme X over any complete non-Archimedean field K, X^an is a good, compact Hausdorff, boundaryless analytic space.
For any K-analytic space Y and complete non-Archimedean extension F/K, the canonical projection Y_F→Y is continuous and surjective.

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, decreasing-FS-net metrics on a fixed semiample Q-line bundle over a projective scheme are stable under finite maxima and decreasing limits, including identically-minus-infinity limits; the continuous subspace is uniformly closed (BE 7.4–7.6).

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, every decreasing-FS-net psh metric on a semiample Q-line bundle over a projective scheme has decreasing smooth semipositive regularization, uniform for continuous endpoints (BE 7.14).

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, PL_R functions on a projective scheme's analytification are uniformly dense in C(X^an); each is a difference of FS metrics on one ample Q-line bundle (BE 5.17–5.18).

On an n-dimensional projective scheme over any complete non-Archimedean field, continuous psh-regularizable metrics on fixed Q-line bundles have symmetric multiadditive positive Radon mixed measures on the fundamental n-cycle, mass (L_1⋯L_n), continuous from uniform tuples to weak measures; their multilinear continuous-dpsh extension is representation independent (BE 8.1).

On good separated boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic spaces over any complete non-Archimedean field, compactly supported smooth forms satisfy Stokes and Green identities. Products of positive (1,1)-forms are positive; α∧Jα is positive for real (1,0)-forms α; integration currents are positive (CLD 3.12, 5.1–5.4).
On projective schemes over any complete non-Archimedean K, continuous psh-regularizable mixed measures commute with complete valued extension F/K: p_*MA_F=MA_K (BE 8.3(iv), 8.4).
